binary_harmonic_grammar.faithfulness_matrix: F is an m by n real matrix
binary_harmonic_grammar.markedness_matrix: M is a symmetric n by n real matrix with zero diagonal
binary_harmonic_grammar.harmony: H_G(x,y)=x F y^T + y M y^T
binary_harmonic_grammar.evaluation: G(x)=y only when y is the unique harmony-maximizing surface representation in S
binary_harmonic_grammar.tie_convention: A tied maximum does not satisfy the source definition of G(x)=y.

network_and_disruption.disruption: delta G is additive, with the markedness block symmetric and zero-diagonal
network_and_disruption.radial_law: Definition 8 specifies a magnitude law mu and a direction uniform on the unit hypersphere
network_and_disruption.error_semantics: Definition 5 calls x-to-z an error when G(x)=y and the disrupted grammar selects z, not merely when z outranks y pairwise.

premises: the two mappings preserve a contrast
their representational difference vectors have equal norm
the intact surface y is less marked than z
matched_pair_result.theorem_3: The normalized intact harmony advantage of y over z for x is strictly greater than that of z over y for w.
matched_pair_result.final_corollary_3: Under spherical disruption, the source states that the marked-to-unmarked selected error is at least as probable as the reverse error.

candidate_support.source_level: The appendix quantifies over an arbitrary declared finite or infinite subset S of binary surface vectors; it does not require S to contain every vector in {0,1}^n.
candidate_support.project_counterexample: SEL-F2 separately instantiates n=2 with all four binary surface vectors. That complete four-candidate inventory and its numerical matrices are project constructions, not source transcriptions.
candidate_support.declared_omissions: The empirical English fragment is expressly incomplete as a theory of English phonology; no complete English candidate inventory is printed.

project_derived_uses: The registered SEL-F2 counterexample retains the source's binary harmony, unique-winner, spherical-direction, equifaithfulness, equidistance, and markedness-asymmetry premises.
The machine proof replaces the source's pairwise crossing event by the conjunction of all target-versus-rival inequalities required by its own selected-output definition.
The project supplies one complete four-output grammar, exact Euclidean and Frobenius onset projections, and one explicit common two-shell spherical law per declared metric.

For each metric, the near shell has positive first-error mass and zero second-error mass, while the far shell contains nonempty open patches of both strict selected-output regions. The exact two-atom mixture makes both named errors positive while preserving the strict reversed order.

two_shell_extension.angular_masses: a is first-event mass on the near shell, b is first-event mass on the far shell, and c is second-event mass on the far shell; a,b,c are strictly positive and second-event near-shell mass is zero

selected_output_mapping_order.first_mapping: input x=(1,0), intact winner y=(1,0), named error z=(1,1)
selected_output_mapping_order.second_mapping: input w=(0,1), intact winner z=(1,1), named error y=(1,0)
selected_output_mapping_order.project_conclusion: P[(G+delta G)(w)=y] < P[(G+delta G)(x)=z] under each constructed common two-shell law

project_instantiation.status: These exact numerical objects are project constructions satisfying the transcribed source contract; they are not attributed to Goldrick and Daland.
project_instantiation.spherical_law: For each declared metric, normalize Haar-induced surface measure on the Euclidean unit sphere and place it on the stated fixed-radius shell.

two_shell_extension.angular_masses: a is first-event mass on the near shell, b is first-event mass on the far shell, and c is second-event mass on the far shell; a,b,c are strictly positive and second-event near-shell mass is zero

scope_ceiling: This transcription records the source's binary HG and noisy selected-output contract. It does not attribute the project counterexample to Goldrick and Daland, does not validate the paper's empirical simulations, and does not refute the source's pairwise Theorem 3 or empirical markedness tendency. The machine-closed common law has a two-atom radial distribution; if an authoritative reading requires an absolutely continuous radial density, the shell result alone is insufficient for that narrower source reading.
